content:
One of the biggest lessons I learned during my legal internship under Senior Advocate Mr. Rajiv Singh at Singh & Aggrawal Association, Dwarka District Court, is that what we study in law school is not just for examinations—it becomes part of real courtroom practice.


When I studied Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 in law school, it was just another chapter in a textbook. But during my internship, I got the opportunity to observe actual cheque bounce matters in court. Because I already understood the legal provisions, it became much easier to follow the arguments, understand the procedure, and connect theory with practice.


That experience made me realize that legal education is incomplete without both strong theoretical knowledge and practical exposure.


Law school teaches us the law. Internships teach us how the law actually works.


To every law student: never ignore your classroom learning, and never miss an opportunity to intern. Both are equally important in shaping you into a better legal professional.


If you ever need law notes, feel free to DM me. I am happy to share them free of cost because I truly believe that sharing knowledge makes the legal fraternity stronger.
